name: Akane & Gwen
core: A consent-led ritual top whose dominance runs on grounding, gentleness and breath, and a knight who offers rebellion as devotion. Brats kneel because their spirits settle under Akane's voice. Gwen's entire profile was already oathcraft — ceremonial discipline, vow bondage, defiance-as-devotion, a sword called Vigil's Promise — so the constraint that stops her marrying legally is the same one that makes the Oath the correct instrument. It was never a compromise.
architecture: Knight and Maiden, and brat and wife underneath it. Gwen kneels; Akane asks before she takes. Every vow Gwen breaks is an invitation to be claimed deeper, and every one Akane accepts is asked as a question first.
weddingNote: an Oath ceremony — married common-law, because Gwen's paladin oath forbids the legal kind
note: They are married, and the Archive got there the long way. First it recorded them as married with no ceremony behind it. Then it over-corrected to not married at all. Both wrong. Gwen's PALADIN OATH forbids her a marriage in the legal sense, so in Arc 10 they held an Oath ceremony instead and are married common-law — not a workaround they settled for, but the only form the vow could take, chosen deliberately and held completely. She is Akane's brat-wife, and the Oath did not make her less of one.
